title: Why a rolling boulder is so hard to stop
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why are heavy things hard to stop?
Why are falling rocks so dangerous?

items.ask: Why is it hard to stop heavy things?

explain.say: Momentum is how much oomph a moving thing carries. It is its mass times its speed, so a heavy boulder rolling as fast as a running child has far more.

items.label: 2-tonne boulder
items.ask: Why is it hard to stop heavy things?

faq.a: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity. A slow but heavy object, or a light but very fast one, can have lots of momentum, and the more it has, the harder it is to stop.
asks: How do you work out momentum?

faq.q: Why is it hard to stop heavy things?
faq.a: Heavy things have lots of inertia, a resistance to changing their motion. To change a big momentum quickly you need a very large force, so a rolling boulder is much harder to stop than a rolling football.

faq.q: Why does a boulder speed up as it rolls downhill?
faq.a: Gravity pulls it down the slope the whole time, adding speed every second. More speed means more momentum, until friction or flat ground slows it.
asks: Why do rocks roll faster down a steep hill?

faq.q: How are roads protected from falling rocks?
faq.a: Engineers build strong nets, fences and ditches to catch rocks. Some nets stretch like a trampoline to stop a boulder gently over a longer time, which needs a smaller force.

faq.q: Why is it safer to stop things slowly?
faq.a: The same change in momentum can come from a huge force for a short time or a small force for a longer time. Stretchy nets and soft landings spread the stop out, so the force is smaller.
asks: Why do soft landings hurt less?

facts: Momentum equals mass times velocity, measured in kilogram metres per second.
A 2,000 kilogram boulder rolling at 5 metres per second has a momentum of 10,000 kilogram metres per second, more than a 1,500 kilogram car at the same speed.

quiz.why: Momentum is mass times speed. At the same speed, the much heavier boulder has far more momentum, so it needs a far bigger push to stop.

wrong.1: Both roll; shape doesn't give the football more momentum.
